battle.name: 塞琉古-帕提亞戰爭
battle.theater: 米底高原與美索不達米亞
battle.brief: 前209年，塞琉古王安條克三世趁帕提亞王密梯里得一世遇弒、新主阿爾達克謝斯一世初立之際，率軍渡幼發拉底深入美索不達米亞，攻陷帕提亞首都赫卡通披洛斯。次年兵敗阿里烏斯河畔，退守底格里斯河畔塞流西亞，因圍軍與城內同時缺糧而被迫突圍撤回敘利亞。希臘重步兵的盾牆體系，正是安條克方陣的底子。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 前209年開戰時，交戰兩方都已成形。塞琉古一方是安條克三世治下的塞琉古王國：王都仍在敘利亞的安條克，疆域自愛琴海東岸一路伸到米底與幼發拉底河東岸。軍隊核心是王室直轄的常備軍，中央為馬其頓式方陣步兵，兩翼配騎兵與象兵，另有各總督轄下提供的分遣隊與外籍雇傭兵；這支軍隊的骨幹，正是卡面這件希臘重步兵所代表的那種互相遮蔽的密集盾牆體系。帕提亞一方是密梯里得一世建立的阿爾薩契德王國：核心在伊朗高原東南與米底，首都赫卡通披洛斯立於米底高原，境內握有美索不達米亞的塞流西亞、泰西封與巴比倫，並延伸至波斯灣沿岸。其軍事支柱是重裝騎兵與弓騎兵，地方防務依托米底城塞與商隊網絡。兩國之外還有一層陰影：羅馬剛在前212年與塞琉古訂立友好條約，帕提亞則在安條克背後向羅馬示好，雙方都清楚這場遠征的成敗會牽動西方。
countriesEn: The war of 209 BC was fought between two states that were already fully formed. On the Seleucid side stood the kingdom of Antiochus III: the royal capital was still at Antioch in Syria, and its territory ran from the eastern Aegean to Media and to the east bank of the Euphrates. The core of its army was the standing force under the king's own command, with a Macedonian-style pike phalanx in the centre, cavalry and elephants on the flanks, and detachments and foreign mercenaries supplied by the satraps; the backbone of that army was precisely the interlocking shield-wall tradition that the Greek hoplite on this card represents. The other side was the Arsacid kingdom founded by Mithridates I, whose heartland lay in south-eastern Iran and Media, whose capital Hecatompylos stood on the Median plateau, and whose territories held Seleucia, Ctesiphon and Babylon in Mesopotamia and reached the shore of the Persian Gulf. Its military pillar was heavy cavalry and mounted archers, and local defence rested on the Median fortresses and the caravan network. A third presence shadowed both: Rome had concluded a friendship treaty with the Seleucids in 212 BC, and Parthia was making friendly advances to Rome behind Antiochus' back, so both sides understood that the outcome of this expedition would be read in the west.
people: 安條克三世此時二十七歲，即位五年，是塞琉古王朝經歷安提柯德姆慘敗之後的重建者。他靠整飭軍紀與收編安提柯系散兵重整軍容，卻未嘗有過遠征米底的經歷。帕提亞王密梯里得一世建國二十餘年，是把部落聯盟變成兩河強權的人，前212年還從安條克二世手中奪下塞琉古的米底總督區；他在前209年死於宮廷陰謀，死因說法不一：波利比亞斯記載他被弒，行兇者疑為近臣貝蘇斯，帕提亞貴族隨後殺死貝蘇斯、改立密梯里得之子阿爾達克謝斯一世，這段記述與後世王表多有出入。執掌阿爾薩契德的是阿爾達克謝斯一世，在位至前186年。實戰層面，帕提亞的指揮落到米底總督安多羅巴祖斯與將領甘吉斯手中；塞琉古方面，弟阿凱俄斯在塞流西亞被圍時策劃脫身，主要戰場上則是安條克本人居中調度。我們今日所知的戰況，主要靠波利比亞斯在《歷史》第八卷的敘述；他於前202年前後抵達塞琉古王宮，記下這場戰爭的經過，也記下安條克負傷與御醫菲利普的軼聞。
peopleEn: Antiochus III was twenty-seven years old and five years into his reign, the restorer of a Seleucid dynasty that had been devastated by the defeat at Antigoneia. He had reformed the army's numbers and discipline and absorbed the stragglers of the Antigonid house, but he had never before campaigned into Media. Mithridates I had ruled for more than two decades and was the man who turned a tribal confederation into a power over the two rivers; in 212 BC he had taken the Median satrapy of the Seleucids from Antiochus II. He was killed in 209 BC in a palace intrigue, and the accounts differ: Polybius writes that he was murdered, the murderer possibly the minister Bessus, after which the Parthian nobles killed Bessus and set up Mithridates' son Artaxerxes I, though that narrative clashes with the later king lists. The Arsacid state was thus headed by Artaxerxes I, who reigned until 186 BC. On the ground, command on the Parthian side fell to the Median satrap Androbazus and to the general Ganges; on the Seleucid side the king's brother Achaeus planned the escape when Antiochus was shut up in Seleucia, and in the battle itself Antiochus directed the army in person. What we know of the campaign comes chiefly from Book VIII of Polybius, who reached the Seleucid court around 202 BC, recorded the course of the war, and preserved the anecdotes of Antiochus' wound and of the physician Philip.
kits: 卡面這件希臘重步兵是方陣的源頭：頭戴科林斯式青銅盔，披青銅胸甲與脛甲，手持約兩公尺長的矛與短劍，背負直徑約九十公分的圓盾；盾牌左右相接即成盾牆，個人於是退入隊形之中。安條克手上的方陣已是它的第三代形態：塞琉古步兵持六公尺左右的白橡木長槍，編為多達十六排的縱深，集結為約五千人的大方陣。帕提亞方面是另一套裝備體系：長矛、平頭標槍、複合弓、青銅或鐵札甲與馬甲，彎刀與投槍用於騎戰，鞍具與馬鐙讓弓騎在高速機動中仍能射擊。攻城與營地器械包括配重投石機、蝎子弩、石弩、雲梯與撞柱，雙方都靠牛車與駱駝隊搬運糧秣、箭矢與攻城器。塞琉古軍營仍沿希臘化宿營傳統掘壕設柵，每日按行軍節奏收放；帕提亞騎兵則以分散駐屯與游擊方式減少糧秣消耗，關鍵時刻才集中成密集的騎兵縱隊。
kitsEn: The Greek hoplite on this card is the ancestor of the phalanx: a Corinthian bronze helmet, a bronze cuirass and greaves, a spear about two metres long with a short sword, and a round shield roughly ninety centimetres across. Once the shields were locked side by side they made a wall, and the individual man disappeared into the formation. Antiochus' phalanx was the third generation of the same idea: Seleucid infantry carried white-oak lances of about six metres, were organised in depths of up to sixteen ranks, and were gathered into great phalanxes of roughly five thousand men. The Parthians fielded a different equipment system, with long spears, javelins, composite bows, bronze or iron scale armour and barding for the horses, curved swords and throwing spears for mounted work, and saddles and stirrups that let horse-archers shoot at speed. Siege and camp equipment included traction trebuchets, cheiroballistae, stone throwers, ladders and battering rams, and both sides moved grain, arrows and siege gear in ox carts and camel caravans. The Seleucid camp still dug ditches and set palisades in the Hellenistic manner, opened and closed to the rhythm of the march; the Parthian horse quartered dispersed and lived off the country to spare their supply lines, and only concentrated into dense columns of horsemen when the moment demanded it.
tactics: 安條克的行軍路線是由敘利亞出發，渡過幼發拉底，再沿兩河間走廊北進美索不達米亞，最後翻越米底高原攻向帕提亞腹地；糧秣全靠從後方遙遠輸送，所以他必須速戰速決。奪下赫卡通披洛斯後，他取走城中財貨與神廟祭器，再向阿里烏斯河推進，試圖切斷帕提亞南北。作戰上，塞琉古仍用老陣法展開：中央是縱深長槍陣，兩翼是騎兵，側翼再放象兵，騎兵先以標槍與箭雨擾亂敵陣，再由方陣承受衝撞。帕提亞避免正面硬撼方陣，先以弓騎在兩翼遊弋消耗，待塞琉古隊形拉開、側翼突出，才以密集重騎縱隊連續衝擊；阿里烏斯河畔的失利，正出在側翼被突破、方陣失去掩護的一刻。安條克退守塞流西亞後反被圍困，城中缺糧，圍城軍營同樣斷糧，兩軍在冬季相持，最後靠計謀與夜色突圍，才渡回底格里斯河對岸。
tacticsEn: Antiochus marched out of Syria, crossed the Euphrates, advanced north through the corridor between the two rivers into Mesopotamia, and then climbed into the Median highlands to strike at the Parthian heartland. All his food came from far behind, so speed was essential. After taking Hecatompylos he carried off the treasure of the city and the plate of its temple, then pressed toward the Arius in the hope of cutting the Parthians north from south. In battle the Seleucids still deployed in the old manner: the deep pike phalanx in the centre, cavalry on the wings, elephants on the flanks, the horse first troubling the enemy with javelins and arrows before the phalanx absorbed the shock. The Parthians avoided frontal collision with the phalanx, screening with mounted archers on both wings until the Seleucid line was stretched and its flanks exposed, and only then charged home in dense columns of heavy horse. The loss at the Arius came at the moment the flank was pierced and the phalanx lost its cover. Shut up in Seleucia, Antiochus was surrounded in turn; the city was short of food, the besieging camp was short of food as well, and the two armies stalemated through the winter until a stratagem and a night movement carried Antiochus back across the Tigris.
data: 現存史料沒有留下這場戰爭可信的雙方兵力數字，這一點必須先說清楚：波利比亞斯寫的是「極多的騎兵」與「不可勝數的軍隊」這類修辭，沒有可核實的名冊。就編制而言，希臘化方陣的標準單位是五千人的大方陣，塞琉古常備軍在順境下約有數萬人，帕提亞能拉出的騎兵數量同樣無從核實；可以確定的是帕提亞把主要力量放在騎兵，而不是攻城用的步兵。時間線是：前209年出兵奪赫卡通披洛斯，前208年兵敗阿里烏斯河並被圍塞流西亞，前206年前後與阿爾達克謝斯一世議和，第三次敍利亞戰爭收場。地理上，從安條克到赫卡通披洛斯的直線距離約一千三百公里，途中要跨越幼發拉底與底格里斯兩道大河；赫卡通披洛斯之名意為「百門之城」，城牆與神廟區是安條克此行最重要的目標。傷亡與損失數字皆無可信記載，唯獨可以確認的是塞琉古遠征軍在歸途中大批耗損，士氣與補給都近於崩潰。
dataEn: The surviving sources give no trustworthy figures for the strength of either side in this war, and that has to be said first: Polybius writes in the language of 'a very great number of horsemen' and 'an innumerable host', with no roll that can be checked. On organisation, the standard Hellenistic unit was the great phalanx of five thousand men, so a Seleucid field army in fair order numbered tens of thousands, while the number of Parthian horsemen cannot be verified at all. What can be said is that the Parthians put their strength into cavalry rather than into siege infantry. The chronology runs: the invasion and the capture of Hecatompylos in 209 BC, the defeat at the Arius and the siege of Seleucia in 208 BC, and a settlement with Artaxerxes I around 206 BC that closed the Third Syrian War. On geography, the direct distance from Antioch to Hecatompylos is about thirteen hundred kilometres, crossing both the Euphrates and the Tigris. The name Hecatompylos means 'the city of a hundred gates', and its walls and temple quarter were the most valuable prize of the expedition. No reliable loss figures survive; what is certain is that the Seleucid army was worn down badly on the march home, with morale and supply both close to collapse.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。第一層是帕提亞王室的變數：密梯里得一世在前209年被殺，繼位者阿爾達克謝斯一世年紀尚輕，宮廷裡還有貝蘇斯奪位的餘波，米底與美索不達米亞的守軍一時失去統一號令，這對塞琉古是天賜的窗口。第二層是邊界糾紛：帕提亞在前212年攻下塞琉古的米底總督區與敘利亞邊境重鎮，等於把手伸進幼發拉底東岸，塞琉古必須把這段邊界奪回。第三層是安條克自己的處境：他剛在安提柯德姆輸掉整個王朝，執政五年只靠整軍維穩，若不在外戰線取勝，王位與朝中都會被懷疑；而他與羅馬的條約讓他以為西方至少不會介入，甚至想像羅馬站在同一邊。第三層加上第一層，便成了遠征米底的理由。帕提亞那邊則把新王的安全與美索不達米亞邊境視為不可退讓的底線，寧可在米底正面迎戰，也不肯讓出赫卡通披洛斯。
causeEn: There were three layers of reason. The first was a change of ruler in Parthia: Mithridates I was killed in 209 BC, his successor Artaxerxes I was young, the aftermath of Bessus' attempted usurpation still unsettled the court, and the garrisons of Media and Mesopotamia temporarily lacked a single command. That was a window the Seleucids could see. The second was the frontier dispute: in 212 BC the Parthians had taken the Seleucid Median satrapy and the strongholds on the Syrian border, which amounted to reaching across the Euphrates, and the Seleucid state had to recover that line. The third was Antiochus' own position: he had lost the whole dynasty at Antigoneia and, five years into his reign, was held together by reorganisation alone; without a victory on the external front his throne and his standing at court would both be questioned. His treaty with Rome also led him to expect that the west would at least stay out, and even to imagine Rome on his side. The third layer, added to the first, produced the march into Media. On the Parthian side, by contrast, the safety of the new king and the Mesopotamian border were a line that could not be given up, and they would rather meet the Seleucids in the field in Media than surrender Hecatompylos.
impact: 這場敗仗的後果遠遠超出戰役本身。安條克回到敘利亞時，軍隊疲憊、士氣低落，王位靠著迅速重整才穩住；方陣萬無一失的觀念也從此被打破，希臘化君主們更清楚正面密集陣線在伊朗高原的騎兵面前多麼脆弱，後來塞琉古對抗羅馬時更加依賴投射武器、象兵與騎步兵混合的編組。前209年的塞琉古還有實力與羅馬在馬其頓分個高下，前190年的曼比亞一戰安條克卻只帶數千殘兵逃回安條克，中間這道轉折線，帕提亞戰爭正是起點之一。對帕提亞而言，此役確立了對美索不達米亞的實際統治，兩河商路與伊朗高原資源連成一體，阿爾薩契德王朝從此穩坐西亞強權位置，並在往後兩百年裡反覆介入塞琉古內鬥。它與漢朝往來、掌控絲路中段，又成為百餘年後羅馬與帕提亞直接碰撞時的對手。換句話說，塞琉古在這場戰爭中失去了主動權，帕提亞則把新得的邊境鞏固成屏障。
impactEn: The consequences of the defeat reached far beyond the campaign. Antiochus came back to Syria with a tired army and broken morale, and his throne survived only because he reorganised quickly. The belief that a phalanx could not be beaten was broken as well, and Hellenistic monarchs came to see how fragile a dense line was against the horse of the Iranian plateau; in the later wars with Rome the Seleucids relied even more on missile troops, elephants and mixed formations of horse and foot. The Seleucid state that could still contest Macedonia with Rome in 209 BC fought the battle of Magnesia in 190 BC with Antiochus escaping with only a few thousand men, and the Parthian war is one of the points at which that line turns. For Parthia the campaign confirmed effective control of Mesopotamia, tied the river lands to the resources of the Iranian plateau, and made the Arsacid dynasty the settled great power of western Asia, from where it intervened repeatedly in Seleucid civil wars over the next two centuries. Its trade with Han China, its grip on the middle of the Silk Road, and the Roman-Parthian collision a century later all grew out of this position. Put plainly, the Seleucids lost the initiative in this war, while the Parthians turned the newly won frontier into a barrier.
result: 前209年，塞琉古攻入米底，奪下赫卡通披洛斯並取走神廟財貨，這是安條克唯一的收穫。前208年，阿里烏斯河之戰中塞琉古中央陣線被帕提亞重騎擊穿，安條克退入塞流西亞，反被圍困；城中與圍城軍營同時缺糧，饑荒成為決定性因素，最後安條克趁夜色與計策突圍，渡底格里斯河回到敘利亞。塞琉古的遠征至此失敗，美索不達米亞與米底重歸帕提亞控制。前206年前後，安條克與阿爾達克謝斯一世議和，並把女兒嫁給這位帕提亞王，把第三次敍利亞戰爭收在美索不達米亞之外；安條克隨即轉向西方，前192年與羅馬開戰，前190年在曼比亞敗北，前188年以阿帕美尼亞條約割讓亞美尼亞。對雙方而言，這場戰爭的直接結果是塞琉古放棄了美索不達米亞，帕提亞則把新得的邊境鞏固成屏障，兩者在西亞的角色從此固定下來。
resultEn: In 209 BC the Seleucids entered Media, took Hecatompylos and carried off the temple treasure; that was Antiochus' only gain. In 208 BC the Seleucid line was pierced by the Parthian heavy horse at the Arius, and Antiochus was driven into Seleucia, where he was besieged in his turn. Famine inside the city and famine in the besieging camp were both decisive, and the siege was finally broken by a stratagem and a night escape that carried Antiochus across the Tigris back to Syria. The expedition had failed, and Mesopotamia and Media returned to Parthian control. Around 206 BC Antiochus made peace with Artaxerxes I and married his daughter to the Parthian king, ending the Third Syrian War short of Mesopotamia. He then turned west, went to war with Rome in 192 BC, lost at Magnesia in 190 BC, and by the Treaty of Apamea in 188 BC ceded Armenia. The direct result of the war was that the Seleucids gave up Mesopotamia, while the Parthians consolidated the new frontier into a barrier, and the roles of the two states in western Asia were fixed from that point on.
